question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\text{E}[\frac{\sqrt{X}}{2}].$

| $x$ | $100$ | $144$ | $196$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{5}{21}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{3}{7}$ |
question.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\sum }_{x\in S}r(x)f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{\sqrt{X}}{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\,f(x) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{100}}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{21}+\frac{\sqrt{144}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{196}}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{7} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{5}{21}+6\cdot \frac{1}{3}+7\cdot \frac{3}{7} \\  & =\frac{25}{21}+2+3 \\  & =\frac{130}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$
